text.p: - Slovenian sport and cultural institutions fear they may lose a significant amount of sponsorship because of the new law which prohibits advertising of tobacco products and trademarks.
- Slovenia is a very promising candidate for full membership to the European Union, EU Commissioner Hans van den Broek said when visiting Ljubljana on Thursday.
- Slovenian parliament should pass a new law on the use of agricultural land by October 13 when the old law expires.
- The growth of wages is seriously hampering Slovenia's economy, president of the Chamber of Economy Jozko Cuk said.
- The government turned down a request from petrol companies to increase petrol prices by about 20 percent.
- Slovenia is expected to sign free-trade agreements with Rumania, Bulgaria, Israel, Lituania and Estonia by the end of this year.
- Although the government formed a special committee in 1993 to determine whether the Catholic Church should partly be financed from the budget, the committee has not yet come up with a decision.
- Slovenian electronic group Iskra managed to reduce its losses significantly in the first half of 1996 due to a 24-percent jump in production.
